common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Chronic blepharitis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Dry eye syndrome without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Chronic recurrent nature typical; unilateral or asymmetric lesion would need biopsy to rule out sebaceous carcinoma.

history.answer: Both of my eyelids have been red, crusty, and burning for about three months now.
It started gradually about three months ago, affecting both eyes from the beginning, and it has stayed constantly bothersome.
The redness is mainly along the edges of my upper and lower eyelids rather than all over the whites of my eyes.
My eyes feel gritty like there is sand in them, and the edges of my lids constantly burn, but there is no deep aching pain inside my eyeball.
My eyesight is completely normal, though occasionally things look slightly blurry until I blink.
No, looking at lights does not hurt my eyes.
No, I have never seen rainbow halos around lights, and I have not had any headaches or nausea.
There is no thick pus, but my eyelids are crusty and stuck together when I wake up in the morning.
Yes, I notice greasy, dandruff-like flakes clinging to the base of my eyelashes every morning.
They itch mildly from time to time, but the burning and gritty feeling is much worse than the itching.
Both my upper and lower eyelids look slightly puffy and inflamed, but there are no painful localized bumps or styes.
No, moving my eyes does not hurt, my eyes do not bulge, and I do not see double.
No, I have not had a cold, sore throat, or fever, and no one around me has had pink eye.
No, I have never worn contact lenses; I only wear reading glasses.
No, I have not had any injury, foreign object in my eye, or exposure to harsh chemicals or welding lights.
No, it does not change with the seasons, and I have never had allergic rhinitis, asthma, or atopic dermatitis.
My eyes do feel dry and tired, especially after staring at computer spreadsheets all day at work, but my mouth is not dry.
No, I do not have morning lower back stiffness, joint swelling, mouth ulcers, or chronic bowel issues.
No, I have never had cold sores around my lips or blisters on my forehead or nose tip.
No, I do not take blood thinners, and I have not had any severe coughing fits, vomiting, or heavy straining recently.
No, I have never had eye surgery, eye injuries, or glaucoma, though my eyelids have felt mildly irritated on and off in past years.
I get mild dandruff on my scalp sometimes, but I do not have facial redness, pimples on my cheeks, or skin rashes.
I usually just splash warm water on my face when showering, but I have never scrubbed my eyelids or used warm compresses.
I was wondering if I might have chronic dry eye disease or perhaps eczema on my eyelids.
I am really frustrated and annoyed by the continuous burning and gritty sensation throughout my working day.
I am hoping to get guidance on how to properly clean my eyelids and perhaps a prescription for soothing drops.
I was diagnosed with high cholesterol a couple of years ago, but I have no other medical conditions.
No, I have never had any surgeries and I have never been hospitalized.
I take atorvastatin 10 mg once daily, and I do not take any over-the-counter medicines or supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only drink one or two beers on social occasions once or twice a month.
I work as an accountant and spend long hours looking at monitors, and I live at home with my wife.
My father had high blood pressure, but there is no family history of eye diseases or blindness.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 122/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.6 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation 98 percent on room air.
Well-appearing, alert male in no acute distress, sitting comfortably.

Visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes, pupils are round and equally reactive to light, full extraocular movements without pain, and bilateral eyelid margins show redness, mild swelling, and greasy flaky collarettes at the base of the eyelashes.
Mild conjunctival redness near the eyelid margins bilaterally, no ciliary flush, and sclerae are clear without hemorrhage or icterus.
Mild scalp flaking present; no facial flushing, telangiectasias, papules, pustules, or eczema.
No preauricular, submandibular, or anterior cervical lymphadenopathy palpable.
No tenderness to palpation over the frontal or maxillary sinuses bilaterally.
